title: prometheus-universal-exporter values
description: Values accepted by the prometheus-universal-exporter chart. Every value has a default, so nothing here is required; the schema exists to catch a typo or a wrong type while rendering rather than after the pod is scheduled. Values that pass a raw Kubernetes shape straight through stay open, so a field Kubernetes gains does not need a chart release.

global.description: Helm's own: the parent chart's global values, which Helm passes to every dependency, an empty map when there are none. The chart reads none of it.

enabled.description: Not read by the chart: the key a parent chart's dependency condition, such as prometheus-universal-exporter.enabled, switches this chart on and off with, which Helm passes on with the rest of the values.

type.description: Not ExternalName: a Service of that type is a DNS alias with no endpoints, so nothing would reach the exporter.

listenAddress.description: host:port. A bare port is rejected here and again while rendering, because Go accepts the flag and then fails to listen with "missing port in address".

watchConfigInterval.description: Rendered as --config.watch-interval: a positive Go duration, such as 60s or 1m30s.

enableLifecycle.description: Rendered as --web.enable-lifecycle when true: enables POST /-/reload.

probeTimeoutOffset.description: Rendered as --probe.timeout-offset when set: how much of Prometheus's scrape timeout a probe leaves unused. Empty keeps the exporter's default, 500ms.

probeDefaultTimeout.description: Rendered as --probe.default-timeout when set: how long a probe without a scrape timeout header may take, whatever timeout parameter it gives. Empty keeps the exporter's default, 30s; 0 leaves such a probe unbounded.

probeMaxConcurrent.description: Rendered as --probe.max-concurrent when set: how many trips to targets, of every collector together, may be in progress at once: a whole number from 0 to 2147483647, as a number or as a string of digits with no zero before another digit. 0 or empty leaves them bounded only per collector.

pythonMaxWorkers.description: Rendered as --python.max-workers when set: how many Python workers, of every collector together, may be alive at once: a whole number from 0 to 2147483647, as a number or as a string of digits with no zero before another digit. 0 or empty leaves them bounded only per script.

shutdownTimeout.description: Rendered as --web.shutdown-timeout when set: how long a stopping pod waits for the probes in progress. Whole hours, minutes and seconds, such as 30s or 1m30s. Empty keeps the exporter's default, 15s.

shutdownDelay.description: Rendered as --web.shutdown-delay when set: how long a stopping pod keeps serving, with /ready answering 503, before the graceful shutdown begins, so Kubernetes takes it out of the Service first. Whole hours, minutes and seconds, such as 5s; 0s turns it off. Empty leaves the flag out.

terminationGracePeriodSeconds.description: The pod's terminationGracePeriodSeconds. Null keeps Kubernetes' 30 unless the shutdown needs more; set, it must be at least server.shutdownDelay plus server.shutdownTimeout plus 10 seconds.

items.description: A whole command-line argument. A flag the chart already renders is rejected while rendering, because Go keeps the last occurrence and the entry would silently win.

enabled.description: Render the static target document and pass it with --static-targets-file.

fileName.description: The static target file's key in the configuration ConfigMap.

path.description: Rendered as --web.static-targets-path: where the static targets' latest results are served. A path of plain segments that no other endpoint uses, and not selfMetrics.path.

expandEnv.description: Rendered as --static-targets.expand-env with enabled: expands ${NAME} environment references in the static target document.

monitor.description: The ServiceMonitor or PodMonitor scraping the static targets endpoint.

targets.description: Static targets this monitor reads, rendered as the endpoint's targets parameter; empty reads every target.

name.description: The monitor is named <fullname>-<name>: a DNS-1123 label, unique among the entries, and neither self nor static-targets, which the chart's own monitors use.

namespaceSelector.description: The namespaces the targets are looked for in, as the Prometheus Operator defines it: any: true for every namespace, or matchNames for a list of them. Without it, the monitor's own namespace.

port.description: The name, not the number, of the port whose address becomes the probe's target, as the Prometheus Operator's monitors take it: a port of the selected Services for type service, a container port of the selected pods for type pod. Lower-case letters, digits and hyphens with at least one letter and no hyphen first or last: up to 63 characters for type service and up to 15 with no two hyphens in a row for type pod. The lengths and the characters are Kubernetes' rules for the name of a Service port and of a container port; the letter is Kubernetes' rule for a container port only, and for type service it is the chart's own rule: a number such as "9115" would be looked for as a name and match no port, so it is refused: name the port and give that name. Kubernetes itself allows a Service port to be named in digits alone, and such a Service cannot be monitored through this value until its port has a name with a letter. Default http.

params.description: Probe parameter overrides. Prometheus Operator params are list-valued, so every entry is a list of strings. collector and target are the chart's own, from .collector and each discovered target's address; setting either fails rendering.

auth.description: The credential Prometheus presents to the exporter on this monitor's scrapes, from a Secret. Enabled, it says which kind, type, and which Secret, secretName; rendering fails without either.

path.description: Rendered as --web.self-metrics-path: the one path the exporter serves its own metrics at, such as /self-metrics or /metrics. A path of plain segments that no other endpoint uses.

type.description: A ServiceMonitor, the default, or a PodMonitor.

goMemLimit.description: Rendered as --runtime.memory-limit-ratio when enabled: the Go memory limit as a share of the container's memory limit, which the exporter reads from its cgroup. GOMEMLIMIT set in env wins.

ratio.description: From 0.1 to 1: below 0.1 the Go memory limit leaves the heap almost nothing and the Go runtime spends its time collecting garbage. 0.5 to 0.95 leaves room for the Python workers; set enabled to false for no limit.

goGC.description: Rendered as the GOGC environment variable of the exporter container when percent is set: the Go garbage collector's target, how far the heap may grow over the live data before the next collection. A whole number from 1 to 10000, as a number or a string, or the string off, which needs a Go memory limit in force; empty or null leaves Go's default, 100. In a values file off needs quotes, since YAML reads a bare off as the boolean false.

livenessProbe.description: Timings of the liveness probe, which checks /health on the http port.

readinessProbe.description: Timings of the readiness probe, which checks /ready on the http port.

autoscaling.description: An optional HorizontalPodAutoscaler for the Deployment, which then leaves replicaCount out. Every replica scrapes every static target, and exports those with export_via_otlp once per replica: keep static targets in a release without it.

podDisruptionBudget.description: An optional PodDisruptionBudget for the exporter's pods; set minAvailable or maxUnavailable, not both.

minAvailable.description: A disruption budget's count: a whole number from 0 to 2147483647, as a number or as a string of digits with no zero before another digit, which is rendered as the number, or a percentage from 0% to 100% with no zero before another digit, as Kubernetes takes it. A string of digits with a zero first would render as YAML's octal number, 010 as eight.

maxUnavailable.description: A disruption budget's count: a whole number from 0 to 2147483647, as a number or as a string of digits with no zero before another digit, which is rendered as the number, or a percentage from 0% to 100% with no zero before another digit, as Kubernetes takes it. A string of digits with a zero first would render as YAML's octal number, 010 as eight.

not.description: Kubernetes refuses a rolling update whose maxSurge and maxUnavailable are both 0, as a number or as 0%: set one of them above 0, or type Recreate, which renders no rollingUpdate. A count left out is Kubernetes' default, 25%.

maxUnavailable.description: Pods that may be missing during a rolling update: a whole number from 0 to 2147483647, or a percentage from 0% to 100% with no zero before another digit, as Kubernetes takes it. A string of digits alone would reach Kubernetes as a string, which it refuses.

maxSurge.description: Pods that may be added during a rolling update: a whole number from 0 to 2147483647, or a percentage of one written with no zero before another digit, as Kubernetes takes it. A string of digits alone would reach Kubernetes as a string, which it refuses.

allowDNS.description: With egress rules, also allow DNS, port 53 over UDP and TCP, to anywhere.

webAuth.description: Mount a Secret's username and password as files for web.basic_auth.username_file and password_file.

successThreshold.description: Kubernetes refuses a liveness probe whose successThreshold is not 1.

readinessProbeTimings.description: As probeTimings, without terminationGracePeriodSeconds, which Kubernetes refuses on a readiness probe.

duration.description: A Go duration such as 30s, 1m30s or 2h.

promDuration.description: A Prometheus duration, as the Prometheus Operator's interval and scrapeTimeout take it: whole numbers of y, w, d, h, m, s and ms in that order, such as 30s or 1m30s, or 0. No fractions, and no us or ns.
